entities.evidence: The Haran who died is identified here as Terah’s son, one of the sons named in Genesis 11:26.
“His father” identifies Terah as the father of Haran.
“In Ur of the Chaldeans” specifies where Haran died, in the land of his birth.
כַּשְׂדִּים names the Chaldean people in the place name “Ur of the Chaldeans.” The source links this geographical qualifier to Chaldea.

review.translation: [And|0] [Haran|1] [died|0] [in|2] [the presence of|3] [Terah|4] [his father|5], [in the land of|6] [his birth|7], [in Ur of|8] [the Chaldeans|9].

analysis.evidence: Haran is the subject of וַיָּמָת. The phrase בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ locates his death in the land of his birth.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol in the third person masculine singular, agreeing with הָרָן (Haran).
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for הָרָן with the root unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 names Haran as the third son listed after “he fathered.” The verse gives no etymology for his name.

analysis.evidence: וַיָּמָת הָרָן means “Haran died.” The phrase תֶּרַח אָבִיו (“Terah his father”) identifies him as the same Haran named among Terah’s sons in Genesis 11:26.
analysis.morphology: Personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix, serving as the subject of וַיָּמָת (“he died”).

analysis.evidence: עַל governs פְּנֵי תֶּרַח אָבִיו, literally “the face of Terah his father.” The phrase places Haran’s death in his father’s presence and indicates that Terah was still alive.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: פְּנֵי is in construct with תֶּרַח, whom אָבִיו identifies as Haran’s father. The phrase עַל פְּנֵי תֶּרַח אָבִיו says that Haran died in the presence of his father Terah.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Haran is the subject of וַיָּמָת, “he died.” In תֶּרַח אָבִיו, “Terah his father,” אָבִיו identifies Terah as Haran’s father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

analysis.evidence: Haran is the subject of וַיָּמָת, “he died.” In תֶּרַח אָבִיו, “Terah his father,” אָבִיו identifies Terah as Haran’s father.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Haran.

analysis.evidence: בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ places Haran’s death “in the land of his birth.” The following phrase בְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים specifies the place as Ur of the Chaldeans.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The common-gender noun אֶרֶץ is singular and stands in construct before מוֹלַדְתּוֹ, “his birth.”

analysis.evidence: בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ means ‘in the land of his birth’. The suffix refers to Haran, and בְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים identifies his native land as Ur of the Chaldeans.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ, ‘his’.

draft.change: Append the place name אוּר to article 2wr at word index 8 under the shared consonantal key אור. The verses establish the geographical sense and leave the name’s etymology open.
draft.definition: Ur, the place called Ur of the Chaldeans where Haran died and from which Terah’s household set out for Canaan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:28 locates Haran’s death בְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים, “in Ur of the Chaldeans”. Genesis 11:31 uses the same name with the preposition מִן to identify the family’s point of departure.

analysis.evidence: בְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים specifies where Haran died. It identifies the place just described as בְּאֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ, “in the land of his birth”.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition בְּ means “in”. Its object is the proper noun אוּר, qualified by the following כַּשְׂדִּים in the place name “Ur of the Chaldeans”.

draft.change: Add the Chaldean gentilic under its consonantal base כשׂד and correct the occurrence’s כרת assignment.
draft.definition: A Chaldean, a member of the people called כַּשְׂדִּים in the plural.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:28 identifies Ur by its association with the Chaldeans. Habakkuk 1:6 explicitly calls the Chaldeans a nation.

analysis.evidence: בְּאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים identifies Haran’s birthplace as “in Ur of the Chaldeans.” כַּשְׂדִּים names the people associated with Ur.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute of a gentilic used as a proper noun. It completes the construct phrase אוּר כַּשְׂדִּים.
analysis.sense: a member of the Chaldean people
